name: Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank
legal_name: Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank Public Joint Stock Company
founded: 1997 (first Islamic bank established in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi; listed on ADX)
ownership_summary: Listed on ADX with 3,632,000,000 shares. At 31 Dec 2025 the only holders above 5% were Emirates International Investment Company LLC (1,431,110,701 shares, 39.40%) and Emirates NBD PJSC (246,223,389 shares, 6.78%); other investors held 53.82%. UAE nationals held 73.3% and foreign investors 26.7% (foreign cap 40%). In Sep 2026 the board proposed an AED 1.75bn rights issue (up to 106.383m new shares at AED 16.45); the investor presentation says major shareholders confirmed full-entitlement participation.
government_link: Not established from opened sources for equity: the ultimate owner of the 39.40% holder (Emirates International Investment Company) was not verified. The Abu Dhabi Government (Department of Finance) holds AED 2bn of Tier 1 sukuk issued on 16 Apr 2009 under the Abu Dhabi bank capitalisation programme. That is capital, not ordinary equity (FY2025 FS).
group_structure: Parent bank in Abu Dhabi (CBUAE) with 61 UAE branches and overseas branches in Iraq, Qatar and Sudan (30 Jun 2026). Wealth and investment subsidiaries: Abu Dhabi Islamic Securities Company LLC ('ADIB Securities', 95%, SCA-licensed equity brokerage) and ADIB Capital Ltd (100%, DIFC, DFSA-regulated asset management, funds, arranging and advisory; described on the board page as the bank's 'investment banking and asset management arm'). Other subsidiaries: ADIB Egypt (53%), Burooj Properties and MPM Properties (real estate), Kawader Services (manpower), ADIB (UK) Ltd, and SPVs incl. Fractionalized Sukuk Holding Limited (ADGM; linked to the Smart Sukuk platform). ADIB Invest 1 (BVI, brokerage) was listed at 31 Dec 2025 but not in the 30 Jun 2026 list. Associates and JVs: Abu Dhabi National Takaful (42%), Bosna Bank International (27%), The Residential REIT (IC) Limited (29%), Saudi Finance Company (51% JV), Abu Dhabi Islamic Merchant Acquiring Company (51% JV) and Arab Link Money Transfer (51%, under liquidation). No subsidiary has its own file, so all figures are group consolidated.

customer_segments: Retail with a focus on UAE nationals (780,000 UAE national customers, which the bank says is over 60% market share) and the mass-affluent segment; Priority Banking (Gold, Diamond); Private Banking (HNW); Business Banking/SME; Wholesale (large corporates, GREs, financial institutions); international via ADIB Egypt.

ADIB Egypt, associates and subsidiaries (16%). Private Banking is a separate reporting segment for HNW clients. The wealth stack includes Wealth Management (advisory, third-party and ADIB-branded funds, structured products, sukuk trading, alternatives), ADIB Securities (brokerage), ADIB Capital (DIFC asset management and investment banking) and the Smart Sukuk digital fractional-sukuk platform.

capabilities.wealth_summary: ADIB runs a broad Shariah wealth stack across Retail Banking (Global Head Amit Malhotra), with a bank-wide Head of Wealth Management hired from HSBC in March 2025 and a separate Private Banking unit (acting head per CG Report 2025). Priority tiers are Gold (AED 250k) and Diamond (AED 750k); holdings at ADIB Securities count towards eligibility. The shelf includes about 14 third-party Shariah funds plus ADIB-branded funds (ADIB Global Sukuk Fund, managed by Azimut in DIFC since Oct 2021), the Khuttati regular-investment plan with four model portfolios, Wakala-based structured products (from USD 30k), secondary sukuk trading (USD 200k per sukuk), and 'ADIB Alternative Investments' (single or co-investments for sophisticated clients). Digital channels include the ADIB Wealth portal (2021), ADIB Securities trading inside the ADIB Mobile App, and the Smart Sukuk fractional-sukuk platform (from USD 1,000; UAE Treasury Sukuk from AED 4,000). ADIB was the first partner bank in the Ministry of Finance's Retail Sukuk programme (Nov 2025). Asset management sits in ADIB Capital (DIFC, DFSA), which launched new products in H1 2026. The Vision 2035 plan (Sep 2026) commits to 'transform the Wealth management franchise into a market-leading, client-centric growth engine'. Wealth AUM is not disclosed; the bank says it grew about 30% over two years.

segments.eligibility: Any one of: deposits/investments with ADIB of AED 750,000; ADIB Securities holdings of AED 750,000; monthly salary transfer of AED 80,000; or ADIB Home Finance of AED 4,000,000

segments.eligibility: Threshold not published; certified private banker assigned

private_banking.detail: ADIB Private Banking: a separate segment in the FS for HNW clients. Each client gets a certified private banker. The offer is a pre-selection of third-party mutual funds and structured products, plus ADIB Securities brokerage. No eligibility threshold is published. CG Report 2025 shows an Acting Head of Private Banking.

asset_management.detail: ADIB Capital Ltd (100%, DIFC, DFSA-regulated) arranges deals, advises on financial products and manages collective investment funds for Shariah vehicles; the board page calls it the 'investment banking and asset management arm'. The H1 2026 MD&A reports 'the launch of new ADIB Capital products' (not named). The ADIB Global Sukuk Fund (DIFC protected cell, launched 4 Oct 2021, min USD 10,000) is managed by Azimut Investment. ADIB also holds 29% of The Residential REIT (IC) Limited. AUM not disclosed.

brokerage.detail: Abu Dhabi Islamic Securities Company LLC (ADIB Securities), 95% owned, SCA licence 604041: ADX and DFM equities with Shariah-compliant stock lists, traded online (e-Trading), by phone or at customer investment centres. The bank calls it 'the number one Islamic brokerage in the UAE' (company claim). ADIB Securities access is now in the ADIB Mobile App. Brokerage fees appear as a line in non-funded income.

digital_investing.detail: (1) Smart Sukuk, which the bank calls 'the UAE's first digitally licensed Fractionalized sukuk investment platform': from USD 1,000, monitored in the ADIB Mobile App; it also distributes UAE Ministry of Finance Treasury Sukuk from AED 4,000 (first bank in the Retail Sukuk programme, Nov 2025). (2) ADIB Securities trading and portfolio view in the ADIB Mobile App. (3) ADIB Wealth portal (launched Oct 2021) with portfolio dashboard, own investment plans and direct trading. (4) Online applications ('10 minutes') for funds, structured products, sukuk portfolio, alternatives and Khuttati.

advisory.detail: Diamond: 'Trusted Advice by a Trusted Advisor' from a trained and certified team, with a research service. Fund selection is supported by Investment Advisors. Wealth Management specialists risk-profile clients for structured products. Private clients get a certified private banker.

discretionary.detail: No discretionary portfolio management mandate found on private banking, priority or wealth pages. ADIB Capital's described DFSA activities are arranging, advising and managing collective investment funds (CG Report 2025).

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Khuttati – My Plan: monthly investment (from AED 1,000) into four Portfolio Solutions (Conservative, Balanced, Growth, Enhanced) or chosen mutual funds; apply online or at a branch. No robo-advisor found.

funds_platform.detail: Third-party Shariah mutual funds, with KFS documents for about 14 distinct funds. Fund names indicate Franklin Templeton, 'Emirates' funds (Emirates India Equity, Emirates Global Sukuk), Comgest, 'Al Ahli' funds (Saudi, GCC, North America), Azimut, Old Mutual, Oasis Crescent and Mashreq Al Islami Income, plus ADIB Global Sukuk Fund and Khuttati. Subscription fee up to 3%. Platform provider not named.

structured_products.detail: ADIB Structured Products: Wakala-based notes on themes such as oil, gold or equity baskets, with exposure to Shariah equities, sukuk and commodities. Minimum USD 30,000, agency fee up to 2%, 3-month lock-in, and protection conditional on holding to maturity.

private_markets.detail: ADIB Alternative Investments: 'single or co-investment with a group of other investors' for 'highly sophisticated clients' willing to lock up capital; no managers or asset classes named. The Diamond wealth page lists private equity, alternative investments and real estate advisory.

islamic_wealth.detail: Fully Islamic bank; products approved by ADIB's Fatwa and Shari'a Supervisory Board and Global Head of Shari'a. Shariah funds, sukuk (primary retail T-Sukuk, fractional and secondary), Wakala structured notes and Shariah-compliant stock lists at ADIB Securities. Industry awards include 'Best Islamic Wealth Manager' (IFN 2025 poll) and 'Islamic Wealth Manager of the Year' (The Asset Triple A).

Hired Basit Sajid Saiyed (ex-HSBC MENAT investments and wealth solutions) as Head of Wealth Management, aiming to become 'the premier Islamic bank for wealth management services'
First partner bank in the Ministry of Finance Retail Sukuk initiative; T-Sukuk sold through the Smart Sukuk platform
H1 2026: first UAE bank licensed as an Open Finance provider (AlTareq TPP); 'new ADIB Capital products' launched; 'strong Wealth Management growth'; 79% of new customers acquired digitally

Vision 2035 and five-year strategy: 'Transform the Wealth management franchise into a market-leading, client-centric growth engine', capture 'growth pools across wealth', scale ADIB Ventures and ecosystem partnerships, embed Gen AI; board proposes AED 1.75bn rights issue

opportunities: Stated strategic priority: Vision 2035 makes transforming wealth management into a 'market-leading, client-centric growth engine' a named pillar, alongside scaling ADIB Ventures and ecosystem partnerships (S6, Sep 2026).
Wealth growth is cited but not measured: 'Wealth AUMs ... +30% over two years' and 'new ADIB Capital products' (H1 2026), with no AUM disclosed (S4, S5).
No discretionary mandates or robo service found; model portfolios exist only inside the Khuttati savings plan (S21, S23, S30).
Private markets offer is generic: 'ADIB Alternative Investments' names no managers or vehicles (S20).
Fresh capital and wealth leadership: AED 1.75bn rights issue proposed (Sep 2026) and a new Head of Wealth Management (Mar 2025) (S6, S35).
barriers: Fully Islamic: every product needs Fatwa and Shari'a Supervisory Board approval (S30, S9).
Already digital in investing: Smart Sukuk fractional platform, ADIB Securities in-app trading and the ADIB Wealth portal (S13, S31, S32).
Own product factories: ADIB Capital (DIFC asset manager) and ADIB Securities (SCA broker), plus an Azimut-managed ADIB-branded sukuk fund (S9, S17).
Leadership gaps to navigate: COO post vacant and private banking head acting (CG Report 2025); no digital/technology head on the published executive committee (S1, S9).
